doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Williams on guitar technique and prison
title: Williams's influences and how he began playing
summary: Williams says he played like Lightning Hopkins and modelled his music on Blind Lemon Jefferson; he started around age 34 after watching Bush Keyes play at suppers.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: And they can't hardly tell the difference. Well, that's why they always told me that they didn't see how I could do it. And my way of going, playing a guitar. So I played like Lightning Hopkins. And I watched my music back like Lion, Lemon, and Jefferson.

Yes. So I met a lot of musicians that they just kind of carried over at the way that I played a guitar. Mm-hmm. And they wanted to learn a couple of my notes to what I was picking when I was in Los Angeles. Well, some man that plays a guitar was way over me, but they just couldn't get that card. So, otherwise, when I started out playing a guitar, it must have been long, about, I'd say, 34, anyway, when I started out. Because I used to go to many supples and watch Bush Keyes play a guitar. Before I ever know what playing a guitar was.
